name: Root
description: Composition Root and Public API Surface for the Apprentice system — Adaptive Model Distillation with Coaching. Serves dual purposes: (1) wires all 9 internal components together via dependency injection following a strict initialization DAG, and (2) defines the public API surface by re-exporting the Apprentice facade class, user-facing types (ApprenticeConfig, TaskResponse, ConfidenceSnapshot, SystemReport), and the error hierarchy (ApprenticeError, BudgetExhaustedError, TaskNotFoundError, LocalModelUnavailableError, AllSourcesUnavailableError). The root owns the component lifecycle (construction order, async resource management via AsyncExitStack, teardown in reverse order), the fine-tuning backend plugin registry (dict mapping FinetuningBackendName → Protocol implementation), and the public __all__ manifest. Inter-component communication uses Pydantic models passed directly (no serialization). State persistence uses model_dump(mode='json') → JSON files. Audit trail uses JSON Lines. CLI output supports human-readable text or JSON. Concurrency model is single-request sequential; budget_manager authorize/record_spend is atomic per request within that model. All internal component errors are caught and translated to user-facing ApprenticeError subtypes before reaching callers. Config validation is strict and fail-fast at startup. No global state — all state flows through the Apprentice instance and its injected dependencies.

functions.name: initialize_composition_root
functions.description: Constructs and wires all 9 components following the strict initialization DAG: config_and_registry → budget_manager → confidence_engine → external_interfaces → sampling_scheduler → router → training_pipeline → reporting → unified_interface. Each phase must complete before the next begins. Uses AsyncExitStack for async resource management. Resolves the fine-tuning backend plugin from config via the BackendRegistry. Component overrides (for testing) replace the default-constructed component entirely. Emits structured lifecycle log entries at each phase. On failure at any phase, tears down already-initialized components in reverse order before raising InitializationError.

functions.name: shutdown_composition_root
functions.description: Tears down all components in reverse initialization order: unified_interface → reporting → training_pipeline → router → sampling_scheduler → external_interfaces → confidence_engine → budget_manager → config_and_registry. For each component: persists state if applicable (budget_manager.force_persist, confidence_engine.persist_state), then closes async resources. The AsyncExitStack is closed after all component-level shutdown. Audit log is flushed before the audit logger itself is closed.

functions.name: resolve_finetuning_backend
functions.description: Resolves a fine-tuning backend plugin implementation from the configured backend name. Uses a simple dict registry mapping FinetuningBackendName string values to constructor functions. The root is responsible for this resolution — the training_pipeline component is backend-agnostic and receives only the resolved implementation. For built-in backends (openai, anyscale, local_lora, axolotl), the registry contains factory functions that construct the backend from config. For 'custom' backends, the registry looks up a custom entry point or raises an error if none is registered.

functions.name: orchestrate_request
functions.description: Top-level request orchestration function documenting the exact call sequence for processing a single run() invocation through all components. This is the contract for how the router (and by extension the Apprentice facade) coordinates all components for a single request. Sequence: (1) Create RequestCorrelation with UUID v4, (2) Look up task in TaskRegistry, (3) Query confidence_engine.get_snapshot for phase/confidence, (4) Query sampling_scheduler.should_sample for routing decision, (5) Query budget_manager.authorize if remote call needed, (6) Execute routing action via router.route (may dual-send via asyncio.gather), (7) If remote was called: budget_manager.record_spend or release_reservation, (8) If coaching sample: confidence_engine.record_comparison, (9) If training data available: training_pipeline.add_example, (10) Budget_manager.record_local_request if served locally, (11) Emit audit log entry via reporting audit logger, (12) Return TaskResponse. All steps carry the RequestCorrelation for audit trail correlation.

invariants: The composition root is the ONLY place where component instances are constructed and wired together — no component constructs its own dependencies internally

Component initialization follows the strict DAG order: config_and_registry → budget_manager → confidence_engine → external_interfaces → sampling_scheduler → router → training_pipeline → reporting → unified_interface. Teardown is reverse order.
All 9 components are non-None after successful initialization. If any component fails to initialize, all previously initialized components are torn down before the error propagates.

Budget enforcement is hard: if budget_manager.authorize() returns allowed=False, no remote API call is made. The system either degrades to local-only or raises AllSourcesUnavailableError if local is also unavailable.

Every remote API call follows the complete budget reservation cycle: authorize (reserve) → API call → record_spend (on success) OR release_reservation (on failure before cost). A crash between authorize and record_spend conservatively counts the estimated cost.
AllSourcesUnavailableError is the ONLY condition under which the system cannot serve a request. It occurs when BOTH local model is unavailable AND remote API budget is exhausted.
Local model failures are graceful — fall back to remote if budget allows, never crash
Budget exhaustion is graceful — fall back to local-only if local is available, never crash
Phase labels are always derived from confidence scores and thresholds — never manually assigned or overridden
Sampling frequency is continuous (float in [0.0, 1.0]), not discrete tiers
Every run() invocation creates exactly one RequestCorrelation with a UUID v4 request_id that is threaded through all component calls for audit trail correlation
Every run() invocation produces exactly one audit log entry, regardless of success or failure
Audit logging failures are captured but never block or delay the response to the caller
No global state — all state flows through the Apprentice instance and its injected dependencies
Config validation is strict and fail-fast at startup. If config is invalid, the system fails immediately with clear error messages. No silent defaults.
The fine-tuning backend plugin is resolved by the root (via BackendRegistry) and injected into training_pipeline. The training_pipeline is backend-agnostic.
Component overrides provided in __init__ or initialize_composition_root completely replace the default-constructed component — no partial merging

Shutdown proceeds through ALL components regardless of individual component errors. Errors are accumulated in ShutdownError, logged at CRITICAL level, but do not prevent other components from shutting down.
State is persisted on shutdown: budget_manager.force_persist() and confidence_engine.persist_state() are called during teardown

Inter-component communication uses Pydantic models passed directly — no serialization between components. Serialization only occurs at persistence boundaries (JSON files) and output boundaries (CLI, audit log).
All timestamps throughout the system are timezone-aware UTC datetimes serialized as ISO 8601 strings. No naive datetimes.
All monetary values use Decimal (stdlib) — never float — to avoid floating-point drift over thousands of micro-transactions
The public API surface (__all__) re-exports types from their owning components — the root does not redefine them. Only AllSourcesUnavailableError and InitializationError are defined at root level.
Files implementing the root component must stay under 300 lines: __init__.py ~10 lines (re-exports), composition.py ~250 lines (initialization/shutdown), errors.py ~40 lines (root-level errors)
